outcomes.text: Understand short recordings about everyday needs, such as shopping, directions and simple instructions.
Work out the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from context.
Identify main points, specific information and details in predictable texts such as advertisements, menus and timetables.
Infer the meaning of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from context.
Use vocabulary for times, days, months and seasons.
Use auxiliary verbs to express obligation, advice, intention, ability, possibility and related meanings.
Express future events with context, 会, 要 and imminent-future patterns such as 要……了, 快要……了 and 快……了.
Reduplicate verbs to indicate a brief or tentative action.
Describe ongoing actions using 呢, 正, 正在, 在 and appropriate negation with 没.
Use 了 to show completed, limited, contrasted or perfective actions, including future sequences and negation.
Use 过 to describe past experiences and negate them with 没.
Use simple directional complements to express movement towards or away from places.
Use result complements to show an action’s outcome.
Use 得 with degree complements to describe how an action is performed.
Use 在 and 到 as postverbs to indicate location or destination.
Use verbal measure words to count occurrences of actions.
Form personal-noun plurals with 们.
Use measure words after numbers, demonstratives, question words and with 些 and 一点儿.
Express possession with 的 and in common noun-noun combinations without 的.
Modify nouns with adjectives or attributives, using 的 where required and omitting it in common combinations.
Use 的 phrases to link modifiers to nouns or nominalise descriptions.
Use common prepositions to express origin, location, association, destination, recipient and means.
Place adverbial phrases before verbs to express time, place, manner, frequency, movement and other meanings.
Use paired or coordinating adverbs to connect information across clauses.
Place time complements after verbs, including constructions with 了 and repeated verbs.
Make comparisons with 比, 跟……一样, 像……一样, 更, 一点儿, 最, quantity complements and 没有.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers up to 10,000, including 二, 两 and approximate quantities.
State years, dates, weekdays and times, including the 24-hour clock.
Refer to time using 的时候, 以前 and 以后.
Construct affirmative sentences with 是, 有, stative verbs and verbless sentence patterns.
Form negative statements with 不是, 没有, 不 and 没 according to the verb or adjective used.
Ask yes-or-no and alternative questions using 吗, verb-not-verb patterns, 是不是, 有没有, 还是 and 吧.
Ask questions with question words, including 谁, 哪, 哪儿, 几, 多少, 为什么, 怎么 and 什么时候.
Use sentence-final 了 to indicate a recent event or changed situation, and negate it with 没有.
Use topic-comment sentences to foreground the subject being discussed.
Use 是……的 to highlight circumstances surrounding a past event.
Describe position with 在, 这儿, 那儿 and location expressions.
Use 着 to show an accompanying action or a state resulting from an action.
Use compound directional complements to describe movement into, out of or down a place.
Use potential complements with 得 and 不 to express whether an action is possible.
Use 地 to form adverbs of manner.
Use 把 to present how an object is handled, including with preceding negators or modal verbs.
Use 被 to form passive sentences, including with preceding negators or modal verbs.
Use 让 and 使 to express causing or allowing someone to do something.
Learn vocabulary for expressing time, dates, seasons, and when events happen.
Learn vocabulary for telling the time, including hours, minutes, quarters, and half-hours.
Learn vocabulary for different parts of the day and related calendar expressions.
Learn vocabulary for weekdays, weekends, and referring to this, last, or next week.
Learn vocabulary for months, years, and referring to previous, current, or future periods.
Learn vocabulary for the four seasons.
Learn vocabulary for getting up, washing, dressing, eating meals, bathing, and going to sleep.
Understand factual information and ideas from announcements, messages, news, interviews and dialogues about familiar subjects.
Discuss activities, hobbies and sport.
Learn vocabulary for hobbies, entertainment, music, arts, reading, social activities, and leisure pursuits.
Learn vocabulary for sports, exercise, competitions, teams, and sporting events.
Understand short, simple texts such as public signs and notices.
Learn vocabulary for shopping, prices, payment, discounts, refunds, customers, staff, money, and opening hours.
Learn vocabulary for measuring distance, length, and weight.
Learn vocabulary for Chinese monetary units.
Use vocabulary for meals, foods, snacks, drinks, cutlery and utensils.
Learn vocabulary for meals, snacks, vegetarian food, and picnics.
Learn vocabulary for common fruits and vegetables.
Learn vocabulary for meat, fish, seafood, and related dishes.
Learn vocabulary for common foods, ingredients, dishes, and seasonings.
Learn vocabulary for snacks, desserts, sweets, and dairy products.
Learn vocabulary for Chinese, Western, Sichuan, Cantonese, vegetarian, and named foods.
Learn vocabulary for alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks.
Learn vocabulary for chopsticks, cutlery, plates, bowls, cups, and spoons.
Learn expressions for liking or disliking food and describing tastes.
Discuss housing, locations, rooms, furniture and household appliances.
Learn vocabulary for homes, buildings, neighbourhoods, cities, rural areas, districts, and locations.
Learn vocabulary for rooms, furniture, household areas, entrances, floors, and household objects.
Learn vocabulary for bathrooms, toilets, towels, toothbrushes, and toothpaste.
Learn vocabulary for common household appliances, including refrigerators, telephones, televisions, and washing machines.
Learn vocabulary for cleaning rooms, doing housework, and washing clothes.
Understand simple descriptions of events, opinions, feelings, hopes and ambitions.
Recognise main ideas, themes, opinions, emotions and attitudes in predictable spoken texts.
Understand simple written descriptions of events, opinions, feelings, hopes and ambitions.
Take part in short social exchanges and communicate about familiar situations to meet simple practical needs.
Describe past experiences, opinions, hopes and ambitions, with brief reasons for opinions and plans.
Identify main points, specific information and details about personal life, family, shopping, school, work and leisure.
Hold unprepared conversations about personal interests and everyday subjects such as family, education, work and travel.
Write linked phrases and sentences about personal life, immediate surroundings and everyday subjects.
Discuss family, relationships, appearance, character and mood.
Learn greetings, apologies, thanks, introductions, farewells, and common conversational phrases.
Learn vocabulary and expressions for inviting people, accepting invitations, and apologising.
Learn vocabulary for family members, relatives, spouses, children, age groups, and forms of address.
Learn vocabulary for describing height, build, hair, eyes, glasses, age, and appearance.
Learn vocabulary for personality, feelings, behaviour, ability, and mood.
Learn vocabulary for names, nationality, ethnicity, gender, age, birthday, contact details, and address.
Understand authentic texts about familiar situations, including articles, emails, blogs and letters.
Recognise main ideas, themes, opinions, emotions and attitudes in predictable written texts.
Communicate with reasonable accuracy using varied structures, time frames and relevant vocabulary.
Link short points into a connected sequence using simple words such as and, but, because and then.
Use suitable strategies to keep conversations going.
Use pronunciation and intonation features to express meaning and attitude.
Complete forms with simple personal details.
Write simple factual information using everyday vocabulary and expressions.
Write connected emails or articles about familiar subjects, including plans, preferences, family, education, work and travel.
Communicate with reasonable accuracy using varied structures, time frames and relevant vocabulary.
Connect short written points using simple linking words such as and, but, because and then.
Discuss digital technology, documents and texts.
Learn vocabulary for computers, mobile devices, online communication, websites, applications, downloads, and social media.
Learn vocabulary for newspapers, books, letters, forms, advertisements, magazines, tickets, and other texts.
Use vocabulary for body parts, health and illness.
Learn vocabulary for major parts of the human body.
Learn vocabulary for illnesses, symptoms, treatment, medical staff, and healthcare facilities.
Use vocabulary for colours.
Learn vocabulary for common colours and shades.
Use vocabulary for clothing and accessories.
Learn vocabulary for clothing, footwear, accessories, uniforms, swimwear, and fashion.
Describe past experiences, hopes and ambitions, giving brief reasons for opinions and plans.
Use vocabulary for travel, transport and finding the way.
Learn vocabulary for travel, transport, tickets, luggage, stations, airports, journeys, and travel arrangements.
Learn vocabulary for maps, directions, distances, crossroads, traffic lights, and turning.
Learn expressions for asking where places are, giving directions, and asking about distance.
Learn vocabulary for famous Chinese cities, landmarks, historic sites, rivers, parks, and cultural attractions.

topics.title: Life in other countries and communities

outcomes.text: Discuss countries, nationalities and languages.
Learn to describe your nationality, country of residence, mother tongue, and foreign languages studied.
Discuss customs, faiths, celebrations, famous sites and cities.
Learn vocabulary for festivals, traditional customs, celebrations, gifts, weddings, fireworks, and greetings.
Discuss continents, countries, nationalities and compass directions.

subtopics.title: People and places – Continents and countries

outcomes.text: Learn vocabulary for continents, countries, international places, and the world.
Discuss nature, the environment, climate and weather.
Learn vocabulary for landscapes, natural features, plants, pollution, recycling, waste, and wildlife.
Learn vocabulary for common domestic, farm, wild, and aquatic animals.
Discuss buildings, local services and shopping.
Use units of length, mass and money.
Learn vocabulary for compass directions, relative positions, and locations.
Learn vocabulary for public buildings, shops, entertainment venues, services, transport facilities, and community places.
Learn vocabulary for post-office services, letters, parcels, envelopes, stamps, postcards, and applications.
Learn vocabulary for banking, saving, withdrawing, exchanging money, and completing bank forms.
Learn vocabulary for losing, finding, taking, stealing, and thieves.

subtopics.title: The natural world and the environment – The climate and the weather

outcomes.text: Learn vocabulary for weather conditions, temperatures, climate, clouds, sunshine, rain, snow, and forecasts.
Discuss educational institutions, school places and people, classrooms, subjects and learning.
Learn vocabulary for nurseries, primary schools, secondary schools, colleges, universities, and academies.
Learn vocabulary for school buildings, facilities, rooms, sports areas, libraries, and accommodation.
Learn vocabulary for students, teachers, classmates, headteachers, pen pals, and exchange students.
Learn vocabulary for classrooms, stationery, books, writing tools, equipment, experiments, and school bags.
Learn vocabulary for lessons, terms, holidays, examinations, homework, revision, clubs, fees, and school activities.
Learn vocabulary for school subjects, Chinese writing, pronunciation, grammar, languages, and learning skills.
Learn expressions for describing ability, difficulty, interest, enjoyment, progress, grades, and improvement.
Discuss jobs, careers and workplaces.
Learn vocabulary for a wide range of occupations and professional roles.
Learn vocabulary for workplaces, companies, jobs, employees, salaries, careers, and retirement.
